title: How the Yellow First-Down Line Works 🏈 #shorts
description:
Watching football this Thanksgiving? That yellow first-down line isn't painted on the field. Each broadcast camera is fitted with sensors that track every pan, tilt, zoom and focus change, and engineers map the field into a 3D model, including its slight curve. Combining the two, a computer knows exactly where the yard line should appear in the shot, recalculating 30 times a second. The trick: the line is only drawn over grass-colored pixels, so players seem to walk right over it. The video is delayed a few frames so the line and picture stay in sync. Sportvision's system debuted on ESPN in the late 1990s.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
